title: X1Pen assembler source, labels and namespaces
summary: X1Pen uses a case-insensitive two-pass Z80 assembler with semicolon comments, global/local labels, optional colonless labels and bracketed namespaces.
syntax: GLOBAL: instruction        global label with colon
GLOBAL instruction         colonless label only at the unindented start of a line
.local: instruction        local label resolved below the latest global label
; comment                  ignored outside a double-quoted DB string
notes: Mnemonics, labels, EQU names, macro names and references are case-insensitive.
Indent instructions when a leading unknown word must not be interpreted as a colonless label.
A local name such as .loop is qualified by the most recent global label. It cannot be used before any global label establishes its scope.
Namespaces are emitted as NAME.SYMBOL. An unqualified reference searches the current namespace, NAME_SPACE_DEFAULT and then matching imported namespace suffixes.
X1Pen injects cold-state address-map symbols before assembly. User labels and EQU definitions may override those predefined values.

examples.title: Global and local labels in the default namespace

title: Numbers, character literals and expressions
summary: Expressions are 16-bit and accept decimal, hexadecimal, binary, ASCII character, symbol and current-address values with arithmetic, shift, bitwise and comparison operators.
syntax: LOW expr / HIGH expr         low or high byte
EXISTS symbol                1 when a symbol is already defined, otherwise 0
notes: Expression results wrap to 16 bits. Division by zero currently evaluates to zero.
Only single-byte ASCII character literals are accepted; use DB with an ASCII double-quoted string for multiple bytes.
Comparisons return 1 or 0 and are primarily useful in #IF/#ELIF.
An unresolved symbol is tolerated as a pass-one placeholder but must resolve during pass two.

examples.title: Build a word from high and low byte expressions
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
VALUE EQU 1234H
DB LOW VALUE,HIGH VALUE
DW (VALUE+2)

title: ORG, EQU, data, reservation and alignment directives
summary: The built-in directives set the origin, define constants and little-endian data, reserve filled bytes and align the current address.
syntax: ORG address                 set location; later ORG may move forward but never backward
NAME EQU expression         define a case-insensitive constant
DB/DEFB item,...            bytes; double-quoted ASCII strings are expanded
DS/DEFS count[,fill]        reserve count bytes; default fill is FFH
ALIGN boundary[,fill]       pad to the next boundary
notes: The first ORG is returned as the assembled block origin. A forward ORG inserts zero padding into the block.
DW is little-endian, matching Z80 memory order.
EQU may forward-reference symbols resolved by the second pass, but cyclic definitions remain errors.
DB string parsing supports double-quoted ASCII text; semicolons inside the string are data rather than comments.

examples.title: Define constants and a small aligned table
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
COUNT EQU 3
DB "X1",0
ALIGN 4,0
DW COUNT
DS COUNT,0FFH

title: Conditional assembly with #IF, #ELIF and #ELSE
summary: A preprocessing pass supports nested #IF blocks, multiple #ELIF/#ELSEIF branches, #ELSE and #ENDIF using assembler expressions and predefined symbols.
notes: Undefined symbols evaluate as zero during conditional preprocessing, so #IF UNKNOWN is false and #IF UNKNOWN==0 is true.
Only active EQU definitions become available to later conditions in the preprocessing pass.
#ELIF after #ELSE, duplicate #ELSE, unmatched directives and unterminated blocks are errors.
X1Pen address-map predefined symbols are available to the preprocessor as bare names and through NAME_SPACE_DEFAULT.

examples.title: Select code using a predefined or user EQU flag
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
TURBO EQU 1
#IF TURBO
  LD A,2
#ELSE
  LD A,1
#ENDIF
RET

title: Parameterized MACRO and ENDM expansion
summary: X1Pen macros use NAME MACRO arg,... through ENDM, support forward calls and calls to other macros, and substitute whole identifier tokens.
notes: A macro call must provide exactly the declared number of arguments.
A macro may call another macro, including one defined later, but recursive expansion is rejected.
Labels, local labels and EQU definitions are forbidden inside a macro body. Put labels on the macro call line or outside the macro.
Macro names cannot conflict with an instruction or directive mnemonic. Nested macro definitions and unterminated definitions are errors.

examples.title: Define and call a register-loading macro
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LOAD8 MACRO REG,VALUE
  LD REG,VALUE
ENDM
START: LOAD8 A,42H
RET

title: Z80 instruction and operand forms accepted by X1Pen
aliases: インデックスレジスタ
summary: The assembler covers documented Z80 base, CB, ED, IX and IY families plus IXH/IXL/IYH/IYL and undocumented SLL/SL1 forms represented in its encoder.
syntax: 8-bit: A B C D E H L (HL); 16-bit: BC DE HL SP AF IX IY; special: I R AF'
conditions: NZ Z NC C PO PE P M; JR accepts NZ Z NC C only
16-bit X1 I/O: LD BC,port then IN r,(C) or OUT (C),r
immediate I/O IN A,(n)/OUT (n),A encodes only the low 8-bit port and is usually wrong for X1 high-byte-decoded devices
notes: Use the symbols list as the accepted mnemonic catalog. Unsupported aliases or alternate syntax produce an assembler error rather than being silently translated.
IXH/IXL/IYH/IYL and SLL/SL1 are undocumented Z80 forms intentionally supported by X1Pen.
Relative JR and DJNZ targets must fit signed -128 through +127 bytes from the following instruction.
For X1 hardware ports such as 1A01H or 4000H, always use the (C) form with the full 16-bit address in BC. IN A,(01H) cannot express 1A01H.

examples.title: Read a full 16-bit X1 port and use indexed addressing
examples.source:
ORG 0100H
LD IX,0200H
LD BC,01A01H
IN A,(C)
LD (IX+1),A
BIT 7,(IX+1)
RET
